newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says he satisfied with Albania poll.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says he satisfied with Albania poll.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Sunday he was "extremely satisfied" with the way elections had been conducted in Albania.

"Apart from one little incident, the elections took place with the greatest possible order and our troops played a very important role in preventing any irregularities or incidents," he told reporters in the northern Italian city of Bologna.
"I want to thank our troops because they've contributed to the greatest expression of democracy a country can have -- free elections.
"We will now ask them to be present and vigilant for the second round, to make that sacrifice."

An official was shot dead in a village near the southern Albanian city of Fier but otherwise Sunday's general election passed off without the widespread violence which has gripped the country for months.
Italy has led the 7,000-strong International Protection Force in Albania since its deployment in April.
